title: INT 10h, the video BIOS
covers: INT 10h, the video BIOS: its calls and their variants.

rows.text: Set video mode.
AL is the desired video mode.
Phoenix and AMI BIOSes return AL as a video mode flag: 20h for a mode above 7, 30h for modes 0-5 and 7, 3Fh for mode 6.
The Phoenix 386 BIOS v1.10 returns AL as the CRT controller mode byte.
It specifies the display mode for the currently active display adapter.
IBM standard modes do not clear the screen if the high bit of AL is set (EGA or higher only).
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x00.
Before the mode set the mouse code is told a new mode comes, SetTrueVideoMode is called with AL, and afterwards the mouse code is told it is done.
On DOS/V in a CJK DOS, AL 0x03, 0x70 to 0x73 and 0x78 set a video mode, call INT10_SetDOSVModeVtext, and fill the screen.
A J-3100 in true video mode 4 or 5 (J3_IsCga4Dcga) gets mode 0x74 set, then INT10_SetJ3ModeCGA4 called with AL.
When J3_IsCga4Dcga() does not hold, AL 0x74 on a J-3100 also fills the screen after the mode is set.
Set text-mode cursor shape.
CH is the cursor start and options: bits 4-0 are the topmost scan line containing the cursor.
CH bits 6 and 5 are the cursor blink: 00 normal, 01 invisible, 10 erratic, 11 slow; on EGA/VGA 00 is normal and any other value is invisible.
CL is the bottom scan line containing the cursor (bits 0-4).
Nothing is returned.
It specifies the starting and ending scan lines occupied by the hardware cursor in text modes.
Buggy on EGA systems: the BIOS remaps the cursor shape in 43 line modes, but returns the unmapped cursor shape.
Applications that change the cursor by programming the hardware directly on EGA or above should call INT 10/AX=1130h, or read 0040h:0085h, first to learn the current font height.
On some adapters an end line greater than the number of lines in the font makes the cursor extend to the top of the next character cell on the right.
CH bit 7 should be zero.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x01, which calls INT10_SetCursorShape.
The shape may be remapped by character height before the CRTC write, with no test of the video mode; the BIOS data keeps it unmapped.
On a machine other than CGA, Olivetti, 3270 or Tandy, with HERC or video control bit 3 clear, CH bits 6-5 equal 01 give CRTC start 0x1E|0x20 and end 0.
On an active video subsystem past the 01 check, with HERC or video control bit 0 clear, a CH or CL with any of bits 7-5 set is written unchanged.
Set cursor position.
BH is the page number: 0-3 in modes 2 and 3, 0-7 in modes 0 and 1, 0 in graphics modes.
DH is the row (00h is top).
DL is the column (00h is left).
Nothing is returned.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x02, which calls INT10_SetCursorPos.
Get cursor position and size.
BH is the page number.
The page number is 0-3 in modes 2 and 3, 0-7 in modes 0 and 1, and 0 in graphics modes.
Phoenix BIOS returns AX as 0000h.
CH is the start scan line and CL the end scan line.
DH is the row (00h is top).
DL is the column (00h is left).
A separate cursor is maintained for each of up to 8 display pages.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x03.
BH selects the cursor position through CURSOR_POS_COL and CURSOR_POS_ROW as given; the case applies no limit by mode.
The case does not set AX; the line that would clear AH is commented out.
Read light pen position (except VGA).
AH is the light pen trigger flag: 00h not down or triggered, 01h down or triggered.
When triggered, DH and DL are the row and column of the character the light pen is on.
When triggered, CH is the pixel row in graphics modes 04h-06h.
When triggered, CX is the pixel row in graphics modes with more than 200 rows.
When triggered, BX is the pixel column.
It determines the current position and status of the light pen, if present.
On a CGA the returned column numbers are always multiples of 2 (320-column modes) or 4 (640-column modes).
Returned row numbers are only accurate to two lines.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x04.
AX is set to 0, so AH always holds 00h; the case comment says the light pen is not supported.
The case reads no light pen state: it only sets AX to 0, and its comment says the light pen is not supported.
The case does not set DH or DL.
The case does not set CH.
The case does not set CX.
The case does not set BX.
The case returns no column number.
The case returns no row number.
Select active display page.
AL is the new page number (00h to number of pages - 1).
Nothing is returned.
It specifies which of possibly multiple display pages is visible.
To learn whether the requested page exists, query the current page with AH=0Fh after this call.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x05; on a Tandy-architecture machine an AL with bit 7 set goes to a case of AL instead of INT10_SetActivePage.
Get CRT/CPU page registers on a PCjr or Tandy 1000.
BH is the CRT page register.
BL is the CPU page register.
The CPU page determines which 16K block of the first 128K of physical memory the hardware maps at B800h.
The CRT page determines the start address of the memory used by the video controller.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x05, then, on a Tandy-architecture machine with bit 7 of AL set, by its case 0x80.
Set CRT/CPU page registers on a PCjr or Tandy 1000.
AL=81h sets the CPU page register.
BL is the CPU page.
Nothing is returned.
The CPU page determines which 16K block of the first 128K of physical memory the hardware maps at B800h.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x05, then, on a Tandy-architecture machine with bit 7 of AL set, by its case 0x81.
The page register byte is written to port 0x3DF and kept in the BIOS data byte BIOSMEM_CRTCPU_PAGE.
Within the Tandy-architecture AL bit 7 block, a PCjr gets BH set to the CRT page and BL to the CPU page whatever AL holds.
Set CRT/CPU page registers on a PCjr or Tandy 1000.
AL=82h sets the CRT page register.
BH is the CRT page.
Nothing is returned.
The CRT page determines the start address of the memory used by the video controller.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x05, then, on a Tandy-architecture machine with bit 7 of AL set, by its case 0x82.
Within the Tandy-architecture AL bit 7 block, a PCjr gets BH set to the CRT page and BL to the CPU page whatever AL holds.
Set CRT/CPU page registers on a PCjr or Tandy 1000.
AL=83h sets both the CPU and the CRT page registers.
BL is the CPU page.
BH is the CRT page.
Nothing is returned.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x05, then, on a Tandy-architecture machine with bit 7 of AL set, by its case 0x83.
Within the Tandy-architecture AL bit 7 block, a PCjr gets BH set to the CRT page and BL to the CPU page whatever AL holds.
Scroll up window.
AL is the number of lines by which to scroll up (00h clears the entire window).
BH is the attribute used to write blank lines at the bottom of the window.
CH and CL are the row and column of the window upper left corner.
DH and DL are the row and column of the window lower right corner.
Nothing is returned.
The call affects only the currently active page.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x06, which calls INT10_ScrollWindow with page 0xFF.
Scroll down window.
AL is the number of lines by which to scroll down (00h clears the entire window).
BH is the attribute used to write blank lines at the top of the window.
CH and CL are the row and column of the window upper left corner.
DH and DL are the row and column of the window lower right corner.
Nothing is returned.
The call affects only the currently active page.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x07, which calls INT10_ScrollWindow with page 0xFF.
Read character and attribute at cursor position.
BH is the page number (00h to number of pages - 1).
In text mode AH is the character attribute.
AL is the character.
For monochrome displays, a foreground of 1 with background 0 is underlined.
The blink bit may be reprogrammed to enable intense background colors, using AX=1003h or the CRT controller.
The foreground intensity bit (3) can switch between character sets A and B on EGA and VGA, allowing 512 simultaneous characters.
In graphics modes only characters drawn with white foreground pixels are matched by the pattern-comparison routine.
Attribute bits: 7 foreground blink or alternate background bright, 6-4 background color, 3 foreground bright or alternate character set, 2-0 foreground color.
Normal colors for 000b to 111b: black, blue, green, cyan, red, magenta, brown, light gray.
Bright colors for 000b to 111b: dark gray, light blue, light green, light cyan, light red, light magenta, yellow, white.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x08, which calls INT10_ReadCharAttr with the address of AX and BH.
Write character and attribute at cursor position.
AL is the character to display.
BH is the page number (00h to number of pages - 1).
BL is the attribute in text mode, or the color in graphics mode.
If bit 7 of BL is set in a graphics mode below 256 colors, the character is XOR-ed onto the screen.
CX is the number of times to write the character.
Nothing is returned.
All characters are displayed, including CR, LF and BS.
A count in CX larger than the positions left in the current row may give an unpredictable result in graphics modes.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x09, which calls INT10_WriteChar with its last argument true.
When the current video mode byte is 0x11, the attribute passed on is BL bit 7 with the low bits 0x3F, whatever BL holds.
Write character only at cursor position.
AL is the character to display.
BH is the page number (00h to number of pages - 1).
BL is the attribute on a PCjr or Tandy 1000 only, or the color in graphics mode.
If bit 7 of BL is set in a graphics mode below 256 colors, the character is XOR-ed onto the screen.
CX is the number of times to write the character.
Nothing is returned.
All characters are displayed, including CR, LF and BS.
A count in CX larger than the positions left in the current row may give an unpredictable result in graphics modes.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x0A, which calls INT10_WriteChar with its last argument false.
Set background or border color, with BH=00h.
Set palette, with BH=01h.
BH=00h selects the background and border color.
With BH=00h, BL is the background and border color (border only in text modes).
BH=01h selects the palette.
With BH=01h, BL is the palette ID: 00h background, green, red and brown or yellow; 01h background, cyan, magenta and white.
With BH=00h nothing is returned.
With BH=01h nothing is returned.
The palette call was only valid in 320x200 graphics on the CGA, but newer cards support it in many or all graphics modes.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x0B, which switches on BH: 0x00 calls INT10_SetBackgroundBorder, 0x01 and any other value call INT10_SetColorSelect.
Any BH other than 0x00, not only 0x01, takes the palette path and calls INT10_SetColorSelect with BL.
Write graphics pixel.
BH is the page number.
AL is the pixel color.
If bit 7 of AL is set, the value is XOR-ed onto the screen, except in 256-color modes.
CX is the column.
DX is the row.
Nothing is returned.
It sets a single pixel on the display in graphics modes.
The call is valid only in graphics modes.
BH is ignored if the current video mode supports only one page.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x0C, which calls INT10_PutPixel.
Read graphics pixel.
BH is the page number.
CX is the column.
DX is the row.
AL is the pixel color.
It determines the current color of the specified pixel in graphics modes.
The call is valid only in graphics modes.
BH is ignored if the current video mode supports only one page.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x0D, which calls INT10_GetPixel with the address of AL.
Teletype output.
AL is the character to write.
BH is the page number.
BL is the foreground color (graphics modes only).
Nothing is returned.
It displays a character on the screen, advancing the cursor and scrolling the screen as necessary.
Characters 07h (BEL), 08h (BS), 0Ah (LF) and 0Dh (CR) are interpreted and do the expected things.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x0E, which calls INT10_TeletypeOutput.
BH is not passed on: INT10_TeletypeOutput is called with AL and an attribute only.
In a DOS/V CJK video mode the attribute passed on is the high byte of the INT10_ReadCharAttr result for page 0, and BL is not used.
Get current video mode.
AH is the number of character columns.
AL is the display mode.
BH is the active page.
If the mode was set with bit 7 set ("no blanking"), the returned mode also has bit 7 set.
EGA, VGA and UltraVision return either AL=03h (color) or AL=07h (monochrome) in all extended-row text modes.
With a Hercules Graphics Card, additional checks are needed: word 0040h:0063h equal to 03B4h for modes 05h and 06h, and bit 1 of byte 0040h:0065h for mode 07h.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x0F.
Only on an EGA or VGA machine is bit 7 of the BIOS video control byte or-ed into AL.
Set single palette register on a PCjr, Tandy, EGA, MCGA or VGA.
BL is the palette register number (00h-0Fh).
BL is also the attribute register number (undocumented), values in table 00017.
BH is the color or attribute register value.
Nothing is returned.
On MCGA only BX=0712h is supported.
Attribute register numbers: 10h mode control (let the BIOS control it), 11h overscan color, 12h color plane enable, 13h horizontal PEL panning, 14h color select.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x00.
On MCGA only AL 0x10, 0x12, 0x15, 0x17, 0x18 and 0x19 pass the machine check; any other AL, this one included, ends the call at once.
Set border (overscan) color on a PCjr, Tandy, EGA or VGA.
BH is the border color (00h-3Fh).
Nothing is returned.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x01.
Set all palette registers on a PCjr, Tandy, EGA or VGA.
ES:DX points to the palette register list.
BH should be 00h to avoid problems on some adapters.
Nothing is returned.
The palette register list is 16 bytes of colors for palette registers 00h to 0Fh, then one byte of border color.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x02.
Toggle intensity or blinking bit.
The call exists on a PCjr, PS, Tandy 1000, EGA and VGA.
BL=00h enables background intensity.
BL=01h enables blink.
BH should be 00h to avoid problems on some adapters.
Nothing is returned.
Before the VGA no function reads the state, but bit 5 of 0040h:0065h holds it; on the VGA use AH=1Bh and read offset 2Dh of the returned data.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x03.
The state is also kept in the global blinking flag, and the text background and text blinking menu items are checked to match it.
On a PCjr, or a machine that is neither EGA nor VGA, the machine check drops AL=0x03 before its case.
Get individual palette register on a VGA, or with UltraVision v2 and later.
BL is the palette or attribute (undocumented) register number, values in table 00017.
BH is the palette or attribute register value.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x07.
BH is read from the register only when BL is at most ACTL_MAX_REG; for a larger BL nothing is read and BH is left as it was.
Read overscan (border color) register on a VGA, or with UltraVision v2 and later.
BH is the border color (00h-3Fh).
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x08.
Read all palette registers and the overscan register on a VGA.
ES:DX points to a 17-byte buffer for the palette register list.
Nothing is returned.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x09.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, which switches on AL to reach each palette function.
Palette functions: AL picks the function, and the machine decides which AL values pass the check before the switch.
An AL that reaches the switch and matches no case logs an error and nothing else.

searched.gave: Not applicable: the DOSBox-X source header of int10.cpp cites no document.
IBM's PS/2 and PC BIOS Interface Technical Reference lists AH=10h and its AL subfunctions. It is a scan, not captured here: NEEDS-OCR.

bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/pc/ps2 holds the May 1988 and April 1987 editions of that reference, and bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/pc/cards the VGA/XGA Technical Reference of May 1992, which describes registers and not INT 10h.
Mirrors of the same bitsavers scans, and a Phoenix System BIOS book that is a third-party summary.
One web search listed Norton Guide transcriptions and a copy of VGABIOS.TXT, both secondary to Ralf Brown's list, which has no section for the AH=10h family itself.

rows.text: Set an individual DAC register on a VGA or MCGA.
BX is the register number.
DH, CH and CL are the new red, green and blue values (0-63).
Nothing is returned.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x10.
The call passes BL, not BX, as the register number.
Set a block of DAC registers on a VGA or MCGA.
BX is the starting color register.
CX is the number of registers to set.
ES:DX points to a table of 3*CX bytes, one byte each of red, green and blue (0-63) per register.
Nothing is returned.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x12.
Select the video DAC color page on a VGA.
BL selects the subfunction: 00h selects the paging mode, 01h selects the page.
BL=00h: BH=00h selects 4 blocks of 64, BH=01h 16 blocks of 16. BL=01h: BH is the page number, 00h-03h or 00h-0Fh.
Nothing is returned.
This function is not valid in mode 13h.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x13.
Read an individual DAC register on a VGA or MCGA.
BL is the palette register number.
DH, CH and CL hold the red, green and blue values.
AX is destroyed by some BIOSes; the Tseng ET4000 BIOS v8.00n always returns AX=00C9h.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x15.
Read a block of DAC registers on a VGA or MCGA.
BX is the starting palette register.
CX is the number of palette registers to read.
ES:DX points to a buffer of 3*CX bytes.
The buffer is filled with CX red, green and blue triples.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x17.
Set the PEL mask on a VGA or MCGA.
BL is the new PEL value.
Nothing is returned.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x18.
Read the PEL mask on a VGA or MCGA.
BL is the value read.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x19.
BH is set to 0 after the call that reads the mask.
Get the video DAC color-page state on a VGA.
BL is the paging mode: 00h four pages of 64, 01h sixteen pages of 16.
BH is the current page.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x1A.
Perform gray-scale summing.
The call exists on a VGA or MCGA.
BX is the starting palette register.
CX is the number of registers to convert.
Nothing is returned.
The RGB values of the registers are converted to grays with the same intensities as the original colors.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x1B.
On MCGA only AL 0x10, 0x12, 0x15, 0x17, 0x18 and 0x19 pass the machine check; any other AL, this one included, ends the call at once.
Set a HiColor graphics mode with the Tseng ET-4000 BIOS.
BL is the video mode: 13h 320x200x32K, 2Dh 640x350x32K, 2Eh 640x480x32K, 2Fh 640x400x32K, 30h 800x600x32K.
BL=3Eh is 640x480x16M (Genoa 7900) and BL=FFh is a Tseng 24-bit color mode.
With BL=FFh, BH is the mode: 2Dh 640x480, 2Eh 640x480x16M, 2Fh 640x400, 30h 800x600, 38h 1024x768??? (Tseng ET4000/W32i).
AL is 10h if supported.
AH is 00h if successful, other on error.
The display is switched into a graphics mode with 15 or more bits per pixel.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x10, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0xF0.
On a VGA only a Tseng ET4000 card with an int10_extensions handler gets the call passed to it, otherwise the default case logs an error.

Get the type of DAC with the Tseng ET-4000 BIOS.
AL is 10h if supported.
BL is the type of digital/analog converter.
It determines which type of digital-to-analog converter is installed on the display board.
BL=00h is a normal VGA DAC and BL=01h a Sierra SC1148x HiColor DAC.
BL=02h is a new Sierra SS24 DAC (24-bit) on a Diamond SpeedStar 24, or a Sierra Mark2 (15-bit) or Mark3 (15/16-bit) DAC with a generic Tseng BIOS v8+.
BL=03h is an ATT20c490/1/2 and BL=04h an AcuMos ADAC1, both 15/16/24-bit.
BL=05h and BL=08h are unknown 15/16/24-bit DACs, BL=06h a Cirrus internal DAC (CL-GD54xx adapters), BL=07h a Diamond SS2410 (15/24-bit).
BL=09h is an unknown 15/16/24-bit DAC; any other value is another HiColor DAC.

Load user-specified patterns into the text-mode character generator, on a PS, EGA or VGA.
ES:BP points to the user table.
CX is the count of patterns to store.
DX is the character offset into the map 2 block.
BL is the block to load in map 2.
BH is the number of bytes per character pattern.
Nothing is returned.
The call causes a mode set, completely resetting the video environment, but without clearing the video buffer.
The current block specifiers may be read with INT 10h AH=1Bh, at offsets 2Bh and 2Ch of the returned data (VGA only).
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x11, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x00.
Load user-specified patterns into the text-mode character generator, on a PS, EGA or VGA.
ES:BP points to the user table.
CX is the count of patterns to store.
DX is the character offset into the map 2 block.
BL is the block to load in map 2.
BH is the number of bytes per character pattern.
Nothing is returned.
The call causes a mode set, completely resetting the video environment, but without clearing the video buffer.
It is designed to be called immediately after a mode set, and is equivalent to AX=110xh except that page 0 must be active.
Bytes per character, max character rows and CRT buffer length are recalculated.
CRTC registers are reprogrammed, R09 being set to bytes/char-1 (max scan line, mode 7 only).
CRTC register R0A is set to bytes/char-2 (cursor start).
CRTC register R0B is set to 0 (cursor end).
CRTC register R12 is set to ((rows+1)*(bytes/char))-1 (vertical display end).
CRTC register R14 is set to bytes/char (underline location), which the list flags as a bug: it should be 1 less.
The current block specifiers may be read with INT 10h AH=1Bh, at offsets 2Bh and 2Ch of the returned data (VGA only).
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x11, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x10.
For AL 0x10 to 0x1F the handler calls Mouse_BeforeNewVideoMode before the switch on AL and Mouse_AfterNewVideoMode after it.
Load the ROM monochrome patterns into the text-mode character generator, on a PS, EGA or VGA.
BL is the block to load.
Nothing is returned.
The call causes a mode set, completely resetting the video environment, but without clearing the video buffer.
The "monochrome" patterns are 8x14 pixels in size.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x11, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x01.
Load the ROM monochrome patterns into the text-mode character generator, on a PS, EGA or VGA.
BL is the block to load.
Nothing is returned.
The "monochrome" patterns are 8x14 pixels in size.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x11, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x11.
For AL 0x10 to 0x1F the handler calls Mouse_BeforeNewVideoMode before the switch on AL and Mouse_AfterNewVideoMode after it.

BL is the block to load.

The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x11, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x02.

BH is the pointer specifier: 00h is the INT 1Fh pointer and 01h the INT 43h pointer.
BH=02h is the ROM 8x14 character font pointer.
BH=03h is the ROM 8x8 double dot font pointer and BH=04h the ROM 8x8 double dot font, high 128 characters.
BH=05h is the ROM alpha alternate (9 by 14) pointer (EGA,VGA).
BH=06h is the ROM 8x16 font (MCGA, VGA).
BH=07h is the ROM alternate 9x16 font (VGA only) (see #00021).
ES:BP is the specified pointer.
CX is the bytes/character of the on-screen font (not the requested font!).
DL is the highest character row on screen.
An alternate font table is an array of a BYTE for the character to be replaced (00h ends the table), then N BYTEs of graphics data, one per scan line.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x11, whose machine check can end the call before the switch on AL reaches case 0x30.
On an MCGA machine BH=0x02 returns the ES:BP of the ROM 8x16 font; on any other machine it returns the ROM 8x14 font.
On an EGA machine BH=0x06 sets ES:BP to the fixed pointer C000:FB80; on a VGA or MCGA it is the ROM 8x16 font.
On an EGA machine BH=0x07 sets ES:BP to the fixed pointer C000:7210; on a VGA it is the ROM alternate 9x16 font.
A BH that matches no case logs an error and sets neither ES nor BP.
The IBM EGA and some other EGA cards return in DL the number of rows on screen, not the highest row number, which the list flags as a bug.
After the switch on BH, CX is read from the BIOS data area character height if BH is at most 0x07, and on a Tseng ET4000 card for any BH.
After the switch on BH, DL is read from the BIOS data area rows byte if BH is at most 0x07, and on a Tseng ET4000 card for any BH.
On an EGA machine DL is the BIOS data area rows byte, as on any other; AX=1121h stores it as one less than the row count.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x11, which switches on AL to reach each character generator function.
On MCGA only AL 0x24 and 0x30 pass the machine check, and on any other machine only an EGA or a VGA does.
For AL 0x10 to 0x1F the handler calls Mouse_BeforeNewVideoMode before the switch on AL and Mouse_AfterNewVideoMode after it.
An AL that reaches the switch and matches no case logs an error, and the switch does nothing else.
